attributes.nuance_translation: A structure which shows one action occuring prior to or in front of another.

attributes.body:
前（まえ）に is used when describing something that is either 'before something' (in time), or 'in front of something' (a location). It is used with verbs (in their non-past form), or nouns. When used with nouns, の is required before 前（まえ）に.

Caution

Another similar construction to 前（まえ）に is 手前（てまえ）に. 前（まえ）に can be used for something that is in front of any location. However, 手前（てまえ）に may only be used when things in front of you (or someone/something else) are being described physically.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: ないうちに and まえに both mean doing something before another event, but with different nuances. まえに simply marks one action happening before another. ないうちに adds the sense of doing something while there's still time. For example, 暗くならないうちに帰ろう means 'Let's go home before it gets dark,' with the nuance that it's better to leave while it's still light out.

first_relatable.title: ないうちに
first_relatable.meaning: Before it becomes, Before ~ occurs, Without

attributes.body: まえに is used to express the relative timing of actions and often follows a plain (non-past) verb to mean 'before doing A.' In contrast, 前者 (the former) and 後者 (the latter) refer to things previously mentioned. They're used to avoid repeating a word or phrase, similar to how we use 'the former' and 'the latter' in English.

first_relatable.title: 前者は・後者は
first_relatable.meaning: The former ~ the latter, The first ~ the second

attributes.body: Both まえに and 手前 can express a meaning similar to ''before' or 'in front of' in English. The difference is that まえに simply refers to happening earlier in time, or being physically located in front of something else. In contrast, 手前 adds nuance, often implying that, because one is faced with a certain situation (A), a particular action or outcome (B) follows as a result.

second_relatable.title: 手前
second_relatable.meaning: Before, In front of, From one's standpoint or side

attributes.body: あとで and まえに are both used to describe the timing of actions, but with opposite meanings. まえに usually follows a plain (non-past) verb and means 'before doing A' (e.g., 食べる前に = 'before eating'). In contrast, あとで typically follows the past tense form of a verb and means 'after doing B' (e.g., 食べたあとで = 'after eating').
